title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-throughput-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Enhances Dedicated autoscaler reporting: adds token-bucket metrics, per-priority throughput guarantees, and utilization breakdowns; improves dashboard graphs and alerting labels.
description: Motivation: customers operating Dedicated fleets asked for clearer visibility into burst and throughput behavior across priority classes and token-bucket smoothing windows. This PR implements additional reporting metrics, improves aggregation logic, and wires the values to the Console dashboards. Summary: add new token_bucket_{capacity,available,refill_rate} metrics, per-priority throughput_guarantee and burst_utilization gauges, and a normalized utilization_series for time-series graphs. Additions include a new collector in autoscaler service, a light-weight aggregation layer that computes 95th/median burst usage, and schema updates for the observability API. Checklist: [x] metric definitions and docs updated, [x] unit and integration tests, [x] Console widgets wired, [x] backward-compatible schema migration. Commits: "Add token-bucket metrics and expose via /metrics"; "Compute per-priority throughput guarantees and smoothing"; "Console: map new metrics to per-fleet dashboard"; "Tests: coverage for edge cases and slow refill behavior". Files changed (high-level): autoscaler/service/collector.go (new collector + aggregation), autoscaler/tokenbucket/tokenbucket.go (expose refill and capacity), observability/api/v1/metrics.go (schema + endpoints), console/dashboards/dedicated_fleet.json (widget definitions), tests/autoscaler/tokenbucket_test.go (new tests), docs/observability/metrics.md (definitions). Testing & CI: unit-tests and integration-tests passed; e2e flaky on first run (timing-related), rerun passed; load-run validated aggregation under 10k req/s simulated workload. Review conversation: Liam requested clearer naming on metric labels (changed _burst_pct to _burst_utilization and added priority label), Riya suggested smoothing window be configurable per-fleet (added config and defaults), Diego flagged a potential double-counting when fallback models trigger burst usage (fixed aggregation to dedupe fallback paths). Merge: approved by all reviewers after two rounds of changes, CI green on final run, merged via squash. Backwards compatibility: metrics endpoint retains old metric names as aliases for one release; no API breaking changes to autoscaler control plane. Impact: improves SLO visibility for Dedicated customers and enables billing/optimization signals for Redwood Optimize. Linear/Jira: references ENG-5421, ENG-5480 and SUP-3345 for customer follow-up.
